raw_response: {"sentences":[{"text":"Settle in.","source_id":"GLUE_PACING","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Stand inside Bowling Green Park at the very foot of Broadway and turn north, up toward the bull.","source_id":"2fe76547-3dc2-4b18-8458-66195c04ebe5","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"From here Broadway runs twelve miles, the longest avenue in America — yet until the second quarter of the nineteenth century the city itself went no farther than City Hall, a fifteen-minute walk north.","source_id":"2fe76547-3dc2-4b18-8458-66195c04ebe5","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"The ground under your feet carries the city's oldest story, because the original Dutch fort stood in this exact spot, and Bowling Green is reputedly where the Dutch struck their deal for Manhattan Island with its Native inhabitants.","source_id":"5dc682e9-2813-4f55-b09a-a14043d27a0e","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0,"also_cites":["c4d24d62-6dd0-4229-bd07-30a1fdb4bed1"]},{"text":"The grand building in front of you is the Alexander Hamilton U.S. Customs House, designed by Cass Gilbert and finished in 1907 — a Beaux Arts colossus with over four hundred and fifty thousand square feet inside.","source_id":"5dc682e9-2813-4f55-b09a-a14043d27a0e","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0,"also_cites":["e2a319b9-32b0-4aeb-af9d-2cc8648d104e","c4d24d62-6dd0-4229-bd07-30a1fdb4bed1"]},{"text":"And it mattered enormously, because before 1913, when Washington first taxed personal income, the federal government ran almost entirely on customs duties from imported goods — and a full seventy-five percent of that money came through the Port of New York, counted right here.","source_id":"5dc682e9-2813-4f55-b09a-a14043d27a0e","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Beaux arts means simply \"fine arts,\" after the great École des Beaux Arts in Paris, but in New York the phrase takes on something larger — buildings that wear their civic pride out loud, grand enough to match what they do, whether they house trains, books, or tax collectors.","source_id":"e2a319b9-32b0-4aeb-af9d-2cc8648d104e","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Today it holds the Smithsonian's museum in the George Gustav Heye Center, spread across two floors, where exhibits of Native literature, language, history, and art fill a splendid elliptical Rotunda lit from above by a glass skylight that weighs a hundred and forty tons.","source_id":"c4d24d62-6dd0-4229-bd07-30a1fdb4bed1","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Before you go in, look up.","source_id":"fbf416d4-f366-4004-a288-f646251923c8","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Twelve figures ring the top, each standing for a great trading nation of history — Greece, Rome, Phoenicia, Genoa, Venice, Spain, Holland, Portugal, Denmark, England, France, and Belgium.","source_id":"fbf416d4-f366-4004-a288-f646251923c8","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Belgium? That one hides a story.","source_id":"fbf416d4-f366-4004-a288-f646251923c8","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"The official line is that during World War I, 'vandals' carved 'Belgium' across a shield that had originally read 'Germany' — and no one has ever explained how vandals could quietly re-cut one of the most visible, most heavily guarded buildings in the city.","source_id":"fbf416d4-f366-4004-a288-f646251923c8","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0}]}
